correctness.rationale: The Cox presentation applies: Shioda–Tate and irreducible fibers give Mordell–Weil rank zero, so Laface–Li Theorem 1.5 applies to the Picard-number-two surface. The equation is integral (the cubic in x has odd degree, so is not a square over C(u,v,z)(x)). On z=0 the x,y derivatives force x=y=0, and all derivatives vanish there. On z≠0 division by z⁶ with x'=x/z², y'=y/z³ gives a product with the one-dimensional torus. At a nonzero base vector, a singularity in the Weierstrass equation would have y'=0 and x'=r a repeated root, with A=−3r² and B=2r³. Squarefreeness of the binary discriminant forces r≠0 and dΔ=108r³(r dA+dB)≠0 in a dehomogenized base coordinate; the latter contradicts the vanishing of the base derivatives. At the zero base vector the sole singular point in this factor is the origin. The four-dimensional hypersurface is thus Gorenstein and regular in codimension one, hence normal by Serre. The plane slice over a smooth fiber is the (1,2,3)-weighted degree-six cone: the projective curve is smooth and avoids the two orbifold points, and the weighted resolution has exceptional line bundle O_E(−1), of degree −1 since the section z cuts the single point at infinity with multiplicity one. This gives the degree-one simple elliptic type, with μ=(6−1)(3−1)(2−1)=10. Its exceptional curve determines j, which has a pole at a simple discriminant zero because A cannot vanish there. The line slice is isolated by the same derivative check and its weights (1,1,2χ,3χ) and degree 6χ give μ=2(6χ−1)² by the regular-sequence Jacobian Hilbert series. No conclusion is drawn about the singular-locus scheme, origin germ, or degenerate plane slices. The frozen symbolic example was inspected, not executed; it is not needed for the universal deductions.

The slices in those same charts have weights (1,2,3) and (1,1,2χ,3χ), with degrees 6 and 6χ. The standard weight product and cone resolution give the displayed Milnor numbers and the elliptic exceptional curve. Reduced discriminant forces a pole in its ordinary Weierstrass j-formula.
